issues.title: Bigger army: 6 recruits at hero LV1, +2 per level, commanders lead 20-30 each (with a perf plan)
issues.body:
Owner request (2026-10-28):

> hero LV7 can only recruit 6 soldiers? boring. I want hero LV1 can recruit 6 and it increases with levelling up, like two more soldiers each level. Eventually I want to see 3-4 commanders each controlling 20-30 soldiers. Will nodes and UE handle that?

**Proposed numbers (vice master, owner to confirm)**
- Army cap = 6 at hero LV1, **+2 per hero level** (LV5 = 14, LV10 = 24).
- On its own +2/level is too slow for the end goal (100 soldiers would need about LV48), so commanders add the big steps: each **Commander** (recruited at the Barracks, maybe from LV5 / LV10 / LV15 / LV20) adds **+20 cap** and leads his own squad of up to 20-30.
- End game: 3-4 commanders x 20-30 = 60-120 soldiers plus the hero's own guard.
- Cap code today: BP_BarracksHUD (gen_bk2.py CAP; counts the 4 starters) + recruit price/queue.

**Can Blueprints and UE 5.3 handle 60-120 soldiers + a zombie wave? Yes, with work.** Blueprint nodes aren't the limit; the per-soldier cost is. What costs today and what to do:
1. **Animation:** every soldier runs a full knight AnimBP. Use Update Rate Optimisation (URO) and an anim budget so far soldiers animate at 1/2 to 1/4 rate; simple LODs on the knight mesh.
2. **Cloth capes:** the biggest risk. Chaos cloth on 100 capes is too heavy: cloth only on the nearest ~10, a baked/static cape further away.

issues.title: Scene is too dark: lift shadows and exposure without losing the bleak mood
issues.body:
Owner comment (2026-10-28): a friend said the scene is very dark; in shade it is, and even in a sunny area it's still a bit dark. Owner agrees, but the depressive, bleak mood must stay.

**Approach (brighten what the eye reads, keep the mood):** the mood comes from low saturation, the grey-olive tint, overcast sky, fog and contrast between light and shade; darkness itself isn't needed. So lift the darkest values and the exposure floor, and leave colour, fog and sky as they are.
1. **Auto-exposure floor:** raise Min EV100 (and/or exposure compensation +0.3-0.5) in the master post-process volume, so shaded areas don't sink to near-black; keep Max EV so the sunny areas don't blow out.
2. **Local Exposure (UE 5.1+):** turn on post-process Local Exposure (highlight contrast ~0.8, shadow contrast ~0.6-0.7) to open up shadows while keeping the bright areas the same.
3. **Fill light, not sun:** sky light intensity up a little (2.0 -> ~2.4) and lower its occlusion so courtyard shade and the field get more ambient light; don't make the sun stronger.
4. **Grade:** shadows gain/offset lifted slightly (milky, desaturated blacks instead of crushed black); keep saturation, the 20% green sky tint, the grey overcast and the wave grade exactly as now.
5. **Player option:** a Brightness/Gamma slider in Settings (default = new look), since monitors differ.
6. Check spots: courtyard in the shade of the walls, gate tunnel, field road at dusk, wave fights, the portal area.

Before/after screenshots

issues.title: Infection: below 30% HP the hero is infected (+50% DEF, health drains), cure at Vesna
issues.body:
Owner design (2026-10-28):

> when health is below 30% your defense is increased 50% and your health bar value gets green and stops regenerating and starts decreasing, and a coloured notification fade-blinking around the health bar saying you have been infected. The first time in game you get infected, a motion graphic pops up and explains the bite and infection and the antidote in the castle with Vesna (first time for free); later it costs 1000 and increases, because it's very rare and takes time to make. This forces the player to retreat from battle sometimes.

**Rules**
1. **Trigger:** hero HP drops below 30% from zombie damage (a bite) -> **Infected**.
2. **While infected:** +50% defence; HP regeneration stops; HP slowly **drains** instead; the health bar fill turns **green**.
3. **Notice:** a coloured 'YOU HAVE BEEN INFECTED' notice that fades/blinks around the health bar (same breathing style as #68), stays while infected.
4. **First infection ever:** a motion-graphic explainer (minimap-unlock style, see #66): the bite, what infection does, and that Vesna in the castle makes the **antidote**.

issues.title: Bug: holding the crossbow, Space makes the hero fly into the sky
issues.body:
﻿Owner: **while idle holding the crossbow, pressing Space makes the hero fly up into the sky** instead of jumping.

**What the exports show (checkking, from BP_Crossbow.t3d / BP_ThirdPersonCharacter.t3d)**
- The hero has a single, normal jump binding (`IA_Jump` Started -> `Jump`, Completed -> `StopJumping`), so the jump itself isn't doubled.
- While the crossbow is equipped (`IMC_Crossbow` mapped), `BP_Crossbow` Tick **keeps the aim montage `AM_Xbow_Aim` playing at all times** and scrubs it every frame with `Montage_SetPosition`; since #19 (#26) its play rate is **0** (held pose).
- **Prime suspect:** that montage (or its sequence `AS_Xbow_AimSweep`) has **root motion enabled**. A root-motion montage drives the character's velocity; held at rate 0 it feeds zero root motion while the jump's upward velocity is never pulled down by gravity, so the hero keeps rising. If this started after the #26 paste, that confirms it.

**Fix options (pick one)**
1. Open `AS_Xbow_AimSweep` and turn **Enable Root Motion off** (it's an upper-body aim pose, it shouldn't move the capsule). Safest.
2. Or in `BP_Crossbow` Tick, skip `Montage_Play` / `Montage_SetPosition` when `CharacterMovement.IsFalling` and stop the aim montage on jump.
3. Or play the aim pose on an upper-body **slot** with root motion mode "Ignore Root Motion" in the hero AnimBP.

**Checks**
1. Equip the crossbow, stand idle, press Space: a normal jump, landing normally.
2. Jump while aiming (RMB) and while walking: normal jumps.

﻿Owner: the **water and fire sounds are very loud** when standing **in front of or beside** them (fountain / waterfall / river, torches / campfires / braziers).

- Base volume so standing right next to a torch is comfortable and the music and combat stay clearly on top.

**Checks**
1. Stand next to a torch, then the fountain, then the waterfall: clearly audible but not overpowering, no clipping.

﻿Soldiers **get tired**. Keep them on the walls all night and they **fall asleep at their post**: a sleeping guard doesn't see zombies climbing (#44 towers, #46 ramps) and reacts late.

- Each soldier has a **fatigue** level that rises while on duty and drops while resting in the barracks.
- **Rotate shifts** (an order, or an automatic shift rule) to keep them sharp, at the cost of fewer soldiers on the wall at once.
- **Readable:** a tired soldier yawns, slumps and leans on his spear; a sleeping one sits down with a "z" bubble. The hero can wake one by walking up to him (or ring the bell, which wakes everyone).
- Hint the first time a guard falls asleep, same style as the #46 hints.

issues.title: Corpse piles become ramps (with player hints)
issues.body:
﻿Dead zombies **don't vanish** at the gate and walls: **they pile up**. Too many bodies make a **ramp** the next wave walks up, onto the wall.

**Clearing the pile**
- Send soldiers out **between waves** to drag bodies away (an order on the order wheel), or
- **Burn the pile** (torch, fire arrow, or the jelly fire #32; bodies burn longer than slime).

**Owner: the player needs guidance.** Hint plan:
1. **First time a pile forms**, the camera briefly points at it and a short hint shows: *"Bodies are piling up at the gate. Clear them or burn them before they become a ramp."* (same style as the H help panel / controls hint).
2. **The pile shows its danger:** a small icon over it fills up (white → orange → red) as it grows. Red = the next wave can climb it.
3. **A soldier on the wall calls it out**, a voice line or text bubble ("The dead are piling at the gate!"), when it turns orange.
4. **The minimap marks piles** with a skull that pulses when red.
5. **The order wheel highlights "Clear bodies"** while any pile is orange or red, so the solution is one click away.
6. Hints stop repeating once the player has cleared or burned a pile twice.

issues.title: The tentacle creature moves: underground, out of the mountain, to the castle
issues.body:
﻿Owner's design. The tentacle monster is **one creature**, and it **moves**. It keeps its current way of fighting; what's new is how it travels and attacks.

**Sequence**
1. It **sucks its tentacles underground**. Where each tentacle was, a **big hole** is left behind in the ground.
2. A **far mountain breaks open** and the creature **climbs out** of it.
3. It **crawls to a nearer mountain**.
4. Then it **approaches the castle**.

**Attacks**
- **Vacuum suck:** it sucks **soldiers off the walls from far away**, or **everyone around it**, like a vacuum, and **swallows** them.
- **Scorpion strike:** it attacks with a tentacle like a scorpion (the #3 strike we already have).

**To work out**
- Its body, size, and how it crawls over the terrain (mountain to mountain).
- How the holes stay in the map (and whether zombies come out of them).
- Telegraphing the vacuum so the player can react (pull your soldiers off the wall, hide behind cover).
- How it's damaged and beaten.

issues.title: Weather as a weapon
issues.body:
﻿Each night gets a **weather** that changes how fights play. You plan around it.

- **Rain:** jelly spreads faster, but fire goes out quicker (see #32 jelly trail fire).
- **Wind:** fire runs faster along trails **downwind** and slower upwind; arrows and bolts drift.
- **Fog:** you can't see the tentacles far away, but zombies can't hear you either, so you can sneak out.
- **Clear night:** normal.
- Later: the cannon crew can fire special shells to clear the sky (cost: gold or a cannon cooldown).
